examples.knowledge_point: Finding the Vector Equation of a Plane Given Its Cartesian Equation
examples.problem: Given the Cartesian equation $2x-y+z+13=0$ of the plane $\Pi,$ find an equation of $\Pi$ in the form $(\mathbf{r}-\mathbf{p})\cdot\mathbf{n}=0.$
examples.worked_solution:
First, from the coefficients in equation of the plane, we get that the normal vector of $\Pi$ is $\mathbf{n}=\langle 2,-1,1 \rangle.$

Now, we solve the Cartesian equation of $\Pi$ for $z\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}2x-y+z+13 & =0 \\ z & =-2x+y-13\end{aligned}
$$

If we put, say, $x=0$ and $y=0,$ we get $z=-13.$ So, the point $P(0,0,-13)$ lies on $\Pi.$ Note that the position vector of $P$ is $\mathbf{p}=\langle 0,0,-13 \rangle.$

Finally, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ (r-⟨0,0,-13⟩)\cdot ⟨2,-1,1⟩ & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem:
Find a Cartesian equation of the plane that passes through the point $P(3,0,-2)$ and is perpendicular to the line 
${\begin{aligned}x=7-2t \\ y=7 \\ z=7t\end{aligned}.$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we note that the position vector of $P$ is $p=⟨3,0,-2⟩.$ From the parametrical equation, we find that the line is parallel to the vector $⟨-2,0,7⟩.$ So, the normal vector of the plane is 

$$
n=⟨-2,0,7⟩.
$$

Using the dot product, we can find the equation of the plane as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨-2,0,7⟩ & =⟨3,0,-2⟩\cdot ⟨-2,0,7⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨-2,0,7⟩ & =-20.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to obtain the Cartesian equation of the plane, we substitute $r=⟨x,y,z⟩$ into the equation above. Hence,

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot ⟨-2,0,7⟩ & =-20 \\ -2x+7z & =-20 \\ -2x+7z+20 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$
